name: ldeep - LDAP Enumeration from Linux
description: ldeep is a Python tool for in-depth LDAP enumeration from Linux. It extracts users, groups, computers, GPOs, trusts, delegations, ADCS templates, LAPS passwords, gMSA passwords, and more. Unlike ldapsearch, ldeep structures output and knows what to look for in an AD context. Complementary to BloodHound for manual deep-dive enumeration.
notes:
=== INSTALL ===
  pip3 install ldeep

=== DUMP EVERYTHING ===
  ldeep ldap -u <user> -p <pass> -d <domain> -s ldap://<dc_ip> all ldeep_output/
  # Creates structured files: users.json, computers.json, groups.json, etc.

=== SPECIFIC QUERIES ===
  ldeep ldap -u <user> -p <pass> -d <domain> -s ldap://<dc_ip> users        # All users
  ldeep ldap ... delegations    # Unconstrained/constrained delegation
  ldeep ldap ... trusts         # Domain trusts
  ldeep ldap ... gmsa           # gMSA passwords (if readable)
  ldeep ldap ... pso            # Password policies (fine-grained)
  ldeep ldap ... silo           # Auth silos/policies
  ldeep ldap ... shadow_creds   # Shadow credentials config
  ldeep ldap ... pkis           # ADCS templates and CAs
  ldeep ldap ... sccm           # SCCM configuration

=== KERBEROS AUTH ===
  export KRB5CCNAME=ticket.ccache
  ldeep ldap -k -d <domain> -s ldap://<dc_ip> users

=== OUTPUT FORMATS ===
  ldeep ldap ... users -o json  # JSON output
  ldeep ldap ... users -o csv   # CSV for spreadsheets

examples.label: Dump all AD data
examples.command: ldeep ldap -u jdoe -p Password123 -d corp.local -s ldap://192.168.1.10 all ldeep_output/

examples.label: Find delegation paths
examples.command: ldeep ldap -u jdoe -p Password123 -d corp.local -s ldap://192.168.1.10 delegations

examples.label: Enumerate ADCS templates
examples.command: ldeep ldap -u jdoe -p Password123 -d corp.local -s ldap://192.168.1.10 pkis

recommended.note: adPEAS is Windows PowerShell; ldeep is Linux Python. Both enumerate AD.

defense.why_it_works: ldeep performs authenticated LDAP queries to enumerate AD objects. Standard domain user credentials provide read access to most AD attributes by default.
defense.prerequisites: Valid domain credentials; network access to LDAP (TCP 389/636).
defense.impact: Complete AD enumeration revealing users, groups, trusts, delegation, ADCS, and other escalation paths.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1087.002] High-volume LDAP queries; enumeration of sensitive attributes (ms-Mcs-AdmPwd, msDS-GroupMSAMembership).
defense.artifacts: LDAP query logs (Event 1644 if enabled); network traffic to DC port 389/636.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=windows EventCode=1644
| stats count by SearchFilter, ClientIP
| where count > 50
| sort -count
defense.sentinel_kql:
SecurityEvent
| where EventID == 1644
| summarize QueryCount=count() by ClientIP=extract(@"Client: (\S+)", 1, EventData)
| where QueryCount > 50
defense.prevention: Enable LDAP query logging (Event 1644); restrict access to sensitive attributes; implement LDAP signing and channel binding.

detections.name: High-volume LDAP enumeration
detections.logic:
SecurityEvent
| where EventID == 1644
| summarize QueryCount=count(), DistinctFilters=dcount(EventData) by ClientIP=extract(@"Client: (\S+)", 1, EventData), bin(TimeGenerated, 5m)
| where QueryCount > 100 or DistinctFilters > 20
detections.false_positives: SCCM, SCOM, or other management tools querying AD; BloodHound collection
detections.tuning: Baseline normal LDAP query volumes; whitelist known management tool IPs
